newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares drift off by close in shortened day.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares drift off by close in shortened day.

text.p: Italian shares closed slightly lower on Monday after giving up earlier gains in a shortened trading day as domestic bonds drifted off their highs and other major world stock markets gave little clear lead to direction.

Technical problems delayed the start of Milan bourse trading until 1310 GMT, while among individual shares Olivetti continued its good run, banks were active on the last day for bids for the Banco di Napoli, while Fiat slipped after a downgrade and ahead of nine-month 1996 figures later today.
The all-share Mibtel index ended off 0.21 percent at 10,305, while the Mib30 closed 0.37 percent off at 15,460.

Fiat was one of the major losers of the day after its recent strong run over the last few weeks from record low levels, and as CS First Boston downgraded its 1996 and 1997 Fiat earnings forecasts due to a poor Italian domestic car market and the high value of the lira.
The shares ended off 3.31 percent at 4,380 lire ahead of expected nine-month 1996 figures later today after a board meeting at the industrial and automotive group.
Among the gainers, Olivetti continued to prosper up 3.55 percent at 581 lire as it continued to build on the stock price rise seen throughout most of last week.

Former state insurer INA came under pressure, off 1.69 percent at 2,205 lire, as it and state-controlled bank BNL said over the weekend that they had made a bid for a stake in loss-making Banco di Napoli. Bids for a 60 percent stake in the bank owned by the Treasury close today.

Banking group Ambroveneto rose 2.94 percent to 3,500 lire due to the reduced likelihood it would bid for the troubled Naples-based bank. BCI continued to gain up 1.04 percent at 2,905 lire after it said last week that it would not bid.
